chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi al-Walid, who said:

I was sitting in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Najiya Abi Habeeb asked him, saying: 'May Allah make me a ransom for you. I have a mill in which I grind (flour). Sometimes I stand during a part of the night, and I know from the mill that the servant has slept, so I strike the wall to wake him up.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, you are in obedience of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seeking His provision.'

key_terms.فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a term of high respect)
key_terms.نَاجِيَةُ: A title/name meaning 'the successful one' or 'the fortunate one'

ai.seo_question: Is working for a living considered an act of worship in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the practice of a servant using the rhythmic sound of a millstone to gently wake a sleeping child, affirming that such mundane labor performed with care for one's household constitutes an act of obedience (*ta'ah*) to Allah. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating daily chores into spiritual life, where the intention of providing lawful sustenance (*rizq*) transforms ordinary work into worship. The hadith underscores the ethical value of diligence and the spiritual significance of seeking provision while maintaining humility and attentiveness to family needs.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abu Al Waleed who said,

‘I was seated in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and Najiya Abu Habeeb asked him<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make me to be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! For me there is a mill wherein I grind (flour). So sometimes I stand during a time from the night, and I know from the mill that the slave has slept, so I strike the wall to wake him up’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, you are within obedience of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, seeking His<sup>azwj</sup> Grace’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from abu al- Walid who has said the following:

“I was sitting in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when Najiyyah abu Habib asked the Imam saying, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, I have a flour-mill. During the night I wake up (for Salah (prayer)) and notice from the mill that the servant is gone to sleep. (Can) I then knock at the wall to wake him up?’ The Imam replied, ‘Yes, you are in the condition of obeying Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, when you are seeking to make a living.’” (Please consult a fatwa also.)
